title: The yogis' seat
hookLine: tradition says the Gorakhnath yogis' center later took Nanak's name, Nanakmata

lines: LEAVE IT BETTER THAN YOU FOUND IT.
A PLACE TAKES A VISITOR'S NAME.
A SEAT THAT BELONGED TO OTHERS.
cards: A campsite sign: leave it better than you found it. A rental apartment with a note on the fridge from the last guests, thanking whoever comes next. Some places even take the name of a visitor who changed them.
That's today's sakhi. The road has carried Guru Nanak and Mardana through oil and enchantment and bitter fruit.
Now it brings them to a seat that belonged to someone else, a center of yogis, and a place that would one day carry a new name. Today: Gorakhmata.

teach.b: The yogis in this story followed Gorakhnath, the teacher their order looks back to, and their center in the foothills was known by his name, Gorakhmata.

We've met Gorakhnath's yogis before this year, on the mountain and at Achal, asking Nanak hard questions. Here, tradition says, the Guru comes to their own home ground and sits down under a dry, dead pipal tree.
And the tree turns green. The yogis are not pleased to find a stranger on their seat. The tellings show them trying their powers to move him, and failing, and then sitting down to talk.
And some of them stay to listen.

teach.h: THE PLACE TAKES A NEW NAME.
teach.b: In time, tradition says, the place itself took the Guru's name: Nanakmata. A gurdwara stands there now, and Sikhs go there as pilgrims. Here's what the story knows.
Nanak doesn't take the yogis' seat by force, and he doesn't tear anything down.

teach.h: NOT ERASED, BROUGHT BACK TO LIFE.
teach.b: The dead tree comes back to life where he sits. The story doesn't mock the yogis; Guru Nanak treated them as serious seekers, worth arguing with because they were in earnest.
His hymns ask them to carry their discipline inward, to make contentment their earrings and the Name their practice.
That's a visitor who leaves a place better: not by erasing what was there, but by making something grow where he sat.

how: Sikhs visit Gurdwara Nanakmata Sahib as a place of pilgrimage and tell the sakhi of the yogis' seat and the pipal tree that turned green.

they fail to move you, and sit down to talk.
you drive them out of their center.
games.why: the tellings say their powers failed, they sat to talk, and some stayed to listen. tradition says the place later took the Guru's name.

practice: Look around you, or think of where you'll be in an hour, a kitchen, a desk, a bus seat, a shared bathroom, and pick one place and one small thing: a wiped counter, a chair pushed in, a note of thanks.
Picture it done, something the next person will find without knowing who did it, and if you pray, say Waheguru as you picture it.
